description: Directory-wide mail capture through the GET-only Graph client: every member user mailbox of the tenant directory (one paged GET /users) except the excluded people (PLX_EXCLUDED_PEOPLE_OIDS / PLX_EXCLUDED_PEOPLE_FILE, integrations/people_exclusion.py; unset or empty, the run refuses before any request) and the HR / payroll deny list (integrations/mail_all_mailboxes_scope.json), both dropped before any request names the mailbox; inbox and sent items over a 90-day first round, then delta, bodies and sha256-pinned attachments in the host's persistent Workbench state (PLX_WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR/mail-all-mailboxes-check, outside the git tree). Two runs share the time budget; run 2 resumes from the stored cursors. excluded_requested is counted on the transport's request log (every URL sent), not on the result set. Then the store is read back offline: every current row carries its owning mailbox's access marking, one mailbox's owner sees that mailbox only, and an actor without a grant sees 0 mailboxes, 0 rows, 0 counts. Counts, booleans and enums only; no names, addresses, subjects or ids.
notes: Live-unverified: never run against real Graph; the evidence label of its tests (integrations/tests/test_capture_mail_all_mailboxes.py) is injected-transport. Requires the host app's User.Read.All (directory listing and lookups) and Mail.Read (an Exchange application access policy may scope mailboxes out: each refused folder is a forbidden gap, the check stays incomplete, never green). Requires PLX_EXCLUDED_PEOPLE_OIDS or PLX_EXCLUDED_PEOPLE_FILE on the host (later_ask excluded-people-oids): without it the command exits 1 with blocked_upstream [{part mail.people_exclusion, source people-exclusion, error_code excluded_people_oids_absent, cause later_ask}] and no request at all; a refused guard or scope listing (HTTP 401/403) is blocked_upstream part mail.directory_listing (permission User.Read.All). ok is the invariants (directory listing complete, excluded_requested 0 on a request log that saw every request, every row owner-marked, owner probe and leak checks); completeness is complete_when runs[*].complete: the first rounds of every mailbox may take several daily runs within the 1500 s budget (a cut folder ends time_budget and resumes from its stored cursor), and the check reads incomplete, never pass, until every folder is current. directory.mailboxes_enumerated >= 7 is the owner's 'more than the six operational mailboxes'. Counts only: mailboxes appear by index, never by id or address.
